spec: Build a REST API for personal notes. Users can create, list, fetch, update and delete notes. Each note has a title, body and timestamps. Notes are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Single DynamoDB-backed entity with ordinary CRUD only.

congruence_checklist: GET endpoint fetching a single note
Note model has title, body and timestamps

plan.summary: A REST API for managing personal notes. Authenticated-by-user-id clients can create, list, fetch, update and delete notes. Each note carries a title, body, and created/updated timestamps, persisted in a single DynamoDB table. Implemented as a FastAPI application deployed as a Lambda function behind API Gateway, with IAM roles and CloudWatch logging.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe returning service status; used by deployment checks.
Create a new note from a JSON body containing title and body; server generates note_id and timestamps.
List notes for the caller, with optional limit and pagination cursor.
Fetch a single note by its identifier; 404 if not found.
Update the title and/or body of an existing note and refresh updated_at.
Delete a note by identifier; returns 204 on success, 404 if absent.

data_models.name: Note
fields: user_id: string (partition key, defaults to 'default-user' when no auth context)
note_id: string (sort key, UUID4 generated server-side)
body: string (0-20000 chars, optional, defaults to empty string)

aws_resources.name: notes-table
aws_resources.justification: Spec explicitly requires notes stored in DynamoDB; table keyed by user_id (HASH) and note_id (RANGE) supports create/fetch/update/delete by id and efficient list-per-user queries.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-function
aws_resources.justification: Hosts the FastAPI application (via an ASGI adapter) as the serverless compute layer for all CRUD endpoints.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-gateway
aws_resources.justification: Exposes the Lambda-hosted FastAPI app as a public REST API with proxy routing for /notes and /health paths.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-lambda-role
aws_resources.justification: Execution role granting the Lambda least-privilege DynamoDB access (GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, Query) on the notes table plus CloudWatch Logs write permissions.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-log-group
aws_resources.justification: Collects Lambda and API Gateway request/error logs for debugging and operational visibility of the CRUD API.

assumptions: No authentication mechanism was specified; the API treats an optional X-User-Id header as the note owner and falls back to a 'default-user' partition value, keeping the data model multi-tenant ready.
'Personal notes' is interpreted as per-user scoping, so listing returns only the caller's notes via a DynamoDB Query on user_id rather than a full table Scan.
Note identifiers are server-generated UUID4 strings; clients cannot supply their own ids.
Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC strings set by the server: created_at on creation and updated_at on creation and every update.
PUT is treated as a partial update (only supplied fields change) since the spec does not distinguish PUT from PATCH semantics.
Listing is paginated with a default limit of 25 (max 100) using an opaque cursor derived from the DynamoDB LastEvaluatedKey.
DynamoDB table uses PAY_PER_REQUEST billing; no provisioned capacity, streams, backups, or global secondary indexes are needed for the described features.
No file attachments, sharing, search, or notification features were requested, so no S3, SQS, SNS, or Secrets Manager resources are planned.

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 8 files — Generated a decoupled FastAPI notes service:

- `models.py` — pydantic models (NoteCreateRequest/NoteUpdateRequest/Note/NoteListResponse/ErrorResponse) with title/body length constraints.
- `storage.py` — abstract `NotesRepository` plus `DynamoDBNotesRepository` (boto3 resource reading `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, region default `us-east-1`, table from `NOTES_TABLE_NAME` defaulting to `notes-table`; conditional writes for 404 semantics; Query-based per-user listing with opaque base64 cursors) and an `InMemoryNotesRepository` fake.
- `app.py` — FastAPI routes for GET /health, POST/GET /notes, GET/PUT/DELETE /notes/{note_id}, `X-User-Id` header scoping with `default-user` fallback, uniform `{detail, code}` error envelope for app errors and validation failures, DI via `get_repository` (overridable in tests), safe `127.0.0.1` uvicorn entrypoint.
- `tests/test_app.py` + root `conftest.py` — fully offline tests using `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` with the in-memory repo injected via `dependency_overrides`, plus a fake DynamoDB table exercising the boto3 repository (CRUD, pagination params, ConditionalCheckFailed → 404/False, other ClientErrors re-raised).
- `requirements.txt` (fastapi, uvicorn, boto3, pydantic only), `requirements-dev.txt` for test tooling, and `README.md` with run/test/LocalStack instructions.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for personal_notes_api covering exactly the plan's aws_resources: a DynamoDB table `notes-table` (user_id HASH / note_id RANGE, PAY_PER_REQUEST, PITR, KMS CMK SSE); a Lambda `notes-api-function` packaged inline via `local_file` + `archive_file` (self-contained CRUD handler for /health and /notes routes, X-Ray tracing, reserved concurrency, KMS-encrypted env vars); an API Gateway REST API `notes-api-gateway` with root + {proxy+} ANY AWS_PROXY integrations, deployment, stage with access logging and X-Ray, and method settings; IAM role `notes-api-lambda-role` with a least-privilege inline policy (only GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/Query on the table ARN, CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents on the specific log group, and scoped KMS use); CloudWatch log groups for Lambda and API Gateway with 365-day retention and KMS encryption. A customer-managed KMS key (with rotation and a non-wildcard-principal key policy) backs encryption for those planned resources. Files: versions.tf (terraform block pinning hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 plus archive/local), variables.tf (defaults matching the plan's resource names), main.tf (provider with project/managed-by default_tags and all resources), outputs.tf.
